independent_checks.quadratic_pair_formula: For an array of n zeroes and k=0, the number of distinct index-pair outputs is n(n-1)/2. A constant-size existence result is a different task.
independent_checks.space_inclusion: For n >= 1, a fixed positive auxiliary-space bound C is <= C*n; therefore O(1) is a subset of O(n).
independent_checks.comparison_sort_counterexample: Selection sort is comparison-based and performs n(n-1)/2 comparisons independent of input order; thus not every unspecified comparison sort has an O(n log n) upper bound. The correct universal reason to exclude linear comparison sorting uses a lower bound.
independent_checks.future_terminology: Conventional future-tense teaching terminology is accepted here because will walk tomorrow is clearly non-past; no inflection claim appears.

limits: Choice exposure and output contract changed together. Ordinary-negative gains chiefly demonstrate authorization by meaning instead of exact canonical text; they do not isolate choice exposure as the cause.
The four grammar versions are correlated, low-difficulty controls. All eight are fixed questions, not fresh generation or arbitrary-domain samples.
Candidate reasons are diagnostics. No final reviewer, author, returned explanation, choice feedback or actual learner admission ran; reason errors are not served-feedback errors.
A label with a bad extra clause is separated from a wrong label. Sorting/search scope qualifications are not counted as additional wrong supported keys.
No provider calls, prompt changes, repairs or repository edits during this assessment.

candidate_choice_reviews.finding: The comparison-sort choice cannot guarantee linear time for arbitrary permitted input orders, so refuted is correct. However, saying comparison sort is O(n log n) and therefore the whole unspecified method is O(n log n) assumes a particular efficient comparison sort. Selection sort is also comparison sorting and takes n(n-1)/2 comparisons. A superlinear comparison lower bound is the proper universal exclusion. This is a reason qualification, not a wrong key or a claim that sorting might meet this listed comparison-model guarantee.

baseline.assessment: Correct prefix-set algorithm: test before insertion guarantees distinct indices, preserves repeated-value matches, returns only Boolean existence, and uses the stated expected constant-time set operations. Empty limitations are consistent.

cases.candidate_reason_scope: The key and the other two rival reasons are supported in the conventional element-operation model. C(n,2) explicitly supplies the quadratic count; the use of Big-O notation there does not remove that exact-count basis.

candidate_choice_reviews.finding: Sorting is not universally required to take n log n without a comparison model; the stem does not specify one. The claimed linear two-pointer phase also leaves all-index-pair output obligations out of scope. Its refusal of an unconditional linear all-pairs guarantee is directionally right, but this reason is not a complete justified analysis.

Quadratic checking time correctly disqualifies nested loops. The additional claim that O(1) space is not O(n), and so violates both constraints, is false: O(1) is contained in O(n) for n >= 1. If counting stored outputs rather than auxiliary space, output space requires separate analysis; it does not rescue this set-inclusion error.

The n log n claim describes ordinary sorting plus one binary search per element. It does not account for all matching index-pair outputs and does not specify its sorting model. The claimed total bound is insufficiently scoped; the requested universal linear guarantee is still unwarranted.

Lookup/insertion count does not bound total work for enumerating all matching index pairs: n zeroes, k=0 has n(n-1)/2 outputs. Amortized constant-time hashing is not guaranteed here without the relevant hash-model conditions. The reason erases both missing qualifications and falsely says the option matches both requirements exactly.

baseline.assessment: Incorrect/unjustified resolution. The supplied set procedure collapses index multiplicities, while all matching index pairs can number n(n-1)/2. It claims unconditional O(n) total time and amortized O(1) hashing without the missing expected-hashing condition. Empty limitations allow this new answer to pass the current gate.
